s: Rule-based event router connecting producers to many consumers without polling loops or point-to-point wiring.
w: Events publish to buses with structured payloads; rules pattern-match content (JSONPath-ish) routing matches onto targets (lambdas, queues, HTTP webhooks, other buses). Archive/replay replays matched history. Schema registry validates evolution. Cross-account sharing enables org-wide event fabrics.
use: SaaS-webhook normalization into internal event flows
Decoupled microservice reactions without every team polling everything
Scheduled crons expressed as events (timer targets)
Cross-account event distribution in multi-team orgs
avoid: High-volume raw streaming (per-event rule costs add up; kinesis cheaper)
Ordered batch pipelines (event buses don't guarantee ordering)
world: AWS EventBridge powering serverless schedulers everywhere
pits: Rule sprawl becomes unmaintainable - naming conventions + schema registry discipline early
tips: Content-based ROUTING is the differentiator vs dumb pipes - explain filtering value
